name: Fitness Tracker
description: This project develops a fitness application aimed at helping users track their physical activities, monitor progress, set fitness goals, and receive personalized workout recommendations. This app is designed to cater to both fitness enthusiasts and beginners, providing valuable tools and insights to support their fitness journey.
rawDescription: This project develops a fitness application aimed at helping users track their physical activities, monitor progress, set fitness goals, and receive personalized workout recommendations. This app is designed to cater to both fitness enthusiasts and beginners, providing valuable tools and insights to support their fitness journey.
highLevelGoals: The App User aims to accurately record and log various physical activities to maintain a comprehensive history of their workouts.
The App User seeks to visualize and understand their fitness journey over time, identifying trends and improvements in their performance.
The App User desires to define specific, measurable fitness objectives and track their advancement towards achieving these targets.
The App User expects to get tailored suggestions for exercises and routines that align with their fitness level, preferences, and goals.
lowLevelGoals: The App User can start recording a new physical activity, specifying its type, to begin tracking real-time metrics.
The App User can temporarily pause an ongoing activity recording, allowing for breaks without ending the session.
The App User can resume a previously paused activity recording to continue tracking from where they left off.
The App User can end an ongoing activity recording, finalizing the session and saving the collected data.
The App User can manually input details for a physical activity that was not recorded by the system, including type, duration, and date.
The App User can modify specific details (e.g., activity type, distance, duration) of a previously recorded or manually added activity.
The App User can remove a specific recorded or manually added activity from their history.
The App User can request a list of all recorded activities within a specified date range.
The App User can retrieve aggregated fitness metrics (e.g., total distance, average pace) for a specified period (e.g., week, month).
The App User can request the generation of a visual graph showing the trend of a specific fitness metric (e.g., running pace) over a selected time frame.
The App User can compare their current performance for a specific metric against historical averages or previous periods.
The App User can filter their activity history and aggregated data to display only specific types of activities (e.g., 'running', 'cycling').
The App User can define a new fitness goal, specifying the target metric, value, and an optional deadline.
The App User can modify the details (e.g., target value, deadline) of an existing fitness goal.
The App User can remove an existing fitness goal from their profile.
The App User can view their current progress towards a specific fitness goal, including percentage completion and remaining target.
The App User can manually mark a fitness goal as achieved, even if the target has not been fully met by the system.
The App User can request workout recommendations tailored to help them achieve a specific, active fitness goal.
The App User can request workout recommendations based on their past activity history and performance data.
The App User can submit feedback on a received workout recommendation (e.g., 'too easy', 'too hard', 'irrelevant').
The App User can save a specific recommended workout routine to their personal library for future access.
The App User can access and view a list of all workout routines they have previously saved.

baselineCritiques.actors: The identified actor "App User" is generic but acceptable as it covers the primary stakeholders (beginners and enthusiasts) mentioned in the description. However, the description implies a system that generates "personalized workout recommendations," which often involves an underlying algorithm or service. While this is typically part of the system itself rather than an external actor, if the system integrates with external data sources (like wearable devices or health APIs), those could be considered actors. Given the text provided, "App User" is the only explicit external entity interacting with the system. The description is clear, and the actor list is not contradictory, but it is minimal. A score of 8 is appropriate because while correct, it lacks specificity (e.g., distinguishing between a "Fitness Coach" if human-in-the-loop was implied, or "Wearable Device" if integration was implied, though the text doesn't explicitly state these). Based strictly on the text, "App User" is the only clear actor.
baselineCritiques.highLevelGoals: The high-level goals accurately reflect the core functionalities described in the software description (tracking activities, monitoring progress, setting goals, and receiving recommendations). They are functional, aligned with the actor's needs, and do not contain contradictions or out-of-context elements. The coverage is complete relative to the provided description.
baselineCritiques.lowLevelGoals: The low-level goals are well-structured, functional, and correctly mapped to the high-level goals. They accurately reflect the actions an actor would take to achieve the strategic objectives (tracking, monitoring, goal setting, and recommendations). However, there is a minor omission regarding the "personalized" aspect of the recommendations. The high-level goal mentions alignment with "fitness level" and "preferences," but the low-level goals only cover requesting recommendations based on goals or history, and providing feedback. There is no explicit low-level goal for the user to define or update their fitness profile (e.g., setting fitness level, preferred exercise types, or constraints), which is a prerequisite for the system to generate truly personalized recommendations based on preferences. Adding a goal like "UpdateFitnessProfile" or "SetExercisePreferences" would improve completeness.
